statements.label: thm:reduced-classification
statements.statement_latex:
[Exact reduced-group classification]
\label{thm:reduced-classification}
Let $G\ne0$ be reduced, and write its length uniquely as
$\lambda=\omega\gamma+n$, where $n<\omega$.
If $n=0$, then $\gamma>0$ and $G$ has exact complexity
$\Pi_{2\gamma+1}$.
If $n>0$, put $H=G_{\omega\gamma}$ and write
\[
 H\cong\bigoplus_{j=1}^{n}C_{p^j}^{(m_j)},\qquad
 m_j\in\mathbb N\cup\{\omega\},\quad m_n>0.
\]
The exact complexity is
\begin{center}
\normalfont
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.62\linewidth}l@{}}
\hline
Condition on $H$ & Exact complexity\\
\hline
$H$ is finite & $d\text{-}\Sigma_{2\gamma+1}$\\[4pt]
Exactly one $m_k=\omega$, and $m_j=0$ for every $j<k$
 & $\Pi_{2\gamma+2}$\\[4pt]
Exactly one $m_k=\omega$, and $m_j>0$ for some $j<k$
 & $d\text{-}\Sigma_{2\gamma+2}$\\[4pt]
At least two $m_j=\omega$ & $\Pi_{2\gamma+3}$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The trivial group has exact complexity $\Pi_1$.

statements.label: thm:bounded-pgroup-classification
statements.statement_latex:
\label{thm:bounded-pgroup-classification}
Let $G$ be a countably infinite Abelian $p$-group of bounded exponent,
and write
\[
 G\cong\bigoplus_{j=1}^n C_{p^j}^{(m_j)},
 \qquad m_j\in\mathbb N\cup\{\omega\}.
\]
Its Scott complexity is determined as follows.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.67\linewidth}|l}
Condition & Exact complexity\\ \hline
At least two $m_j$ equal $\omega$ & $\Pi_3$\\
Exactly one $m_k=\omega$, and some $m_j>0$ with $j<k$
 & $d\text{-}\Sigma_2$\\
Exactly one $m_k=\omega$, and all $m_j=0$ with $j<k$
 & $\Pi_2$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Thus no bounded-exponent countable Abelian $p$-group has an exact
pure $\Sigma$ Scott complexity. The case of at least two infinite
multiplicities is \cite[Theorem~4.2]{ACM}; the proof below supplies
the remaining cases, including arbitrary finite summands above the
unique infinite multiplicity.

statements.label: lem:prescribed-tail
statements.statement_latex:
[Transfinite prescribed-tail existence]
\label{lem:prescribed-tail}
Let $\gamma>0$ be countable, put $\delta=\omega\gamma$, and let $G$
be a countable reduced Abelian $p$-group of length at least $\delta$.
For every nonzero countable reduced $p$-group $T$ there is a countable
reduced $p$-group $H(T)$ such that
\[
 u_{H(T)}(\xi)=u_G(\xi)\quad(\xi<\delta),
 \qquad H(T)_\delta\cong T.
\]
Its length is $\delta+\lambda_T$.

statements.label: lem:quotient-filtration
statements.statement_latex:
[Quotient filtration below a limit]
\label{lem:quotient-filtration}
Let $\delta=\omega\gamma$ and $T\le G_\delta$. For the quotient
map $q:G\to Q=G/T$, one has
\[
 Q_\alpha=q(G_\alpha)\quad(\alpha\le\delta).
\]
For every $\beta<\delta$, $q$ induces an isomorphism of the
$\beta$-th Ulm quotients, so $u_Q(\beta)=u_G(\beta)$.

statements.label: lem:products
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite-product preservation]\label{lem:products}
If $(A_i,\bar a_i)\leq_\alpha(B_i,\bar b_i)$ for $i=1,2$, then
\[
 (A_1\oplus A_2,(\bar a_1,\bar a_2))
 \leq_\alpha
 (B_1\oplus B_2,(\bar b_1,\bar b_2)).
\]
The paired notation denotes componentwise pairing of corresponding
entries into tuples of product elements.

statements.label: thm:odd-obstruction
statements.statement_latex:
\label{thm:odd-obstruction}
Let $\gamma>0$ be countable. If $G=R\oplus D$, with $R$ reduced and
$D$ divisible, and $\lambda_R\ge\omega\gamma$, then $G$ has no
$\Sigma_{2\gamma+1}$ Scott sentence. No countable Abelian
$p$-group has exact pure $\Sigma_{2\gamma+1}$ complexity.

statements.label: lem:absorption
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite support absorption]
\label{lem:absorption}
Suppose $H=K\oplus T$ is bounded, $p^kT=0$, and a cyclic decomposition of
$K$ contains infinitely many $C_{p^k}$ summands. Then
$K\preceq_{\Sigma_1}H$, for ordinary infinitary formulas with parameters
from $K$. Consequently $H\le_2K$.

statements.label: lem:terminal-deletion
statements.statement_latex:
[Deleting a terminal direct summand]
\label{lem:terminal-deletion}
Put $\delta=\omega\gamma$, where $\gamma\ge0$, and suppose $G$ is reduced
with nonzero bounded $H=G_\delta$. Write $H=K\oplus T$, assume $K$ has
the same exponent as $H$, and put $Q=G/T$, with quotient map $q$.
For $A=\langle\bar a\rangle$ finite, suppose $A\cap H\subseteq K$.
Then
\[
 u_Q(\xi)=u_G(\xi)\quad(\xi<\delta),\qquad Q_\delta\cong K,\qquad
 \lambda_Q=\lambda_G,
\]
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-deletion}
             (G,\bar a)\le_{2\gamma+1}(Q,q\bar a).
\end{equation}
If also $H\le_2K$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:even-deletion}
                         G\le_{2\gamma+2}Q.
\end{equation}

statements.label: lem:walker-filtration
statements.statement_latex:
\label{lem:walker-filtration}
Every element of $W_\xi$ has a unique finite expression
\[
 \sum_s c_s e_s,\qquad 0\le c_s<p.
\]
Moreover, for every ordinal $\alpha$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:walker-filtration}
 (W_\xi)_\alpha
 =\left\langle e_s:\operatorname{last}(s)\ge\alpha\right\rangle.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
 (W_\xi)_\xi=\langle e_{(\xi)}\rangle\cong C_p,
 \qquad (W_\xi)_{\xi+1}=0.
\]
For every ordinal $\delta$,
\[
 (W_{\delta+1})_\delta\cong C_{p^2}.
\]

statements.label: thm:difference-spectrum
statements.statement_latex:
[The difference spectrum]\label{thm:difference-spectrum}
Every positive countable successor $d\text{-}\Sigma_\alpha$ complexity
occurs among countable reduced abelian $p$-groups. Among infinite such
groups the attained difference levels are exactly the successors
$\alpha\geq2$.

statements.label: lem:infinite-divisible-bf
statements.statement_latex:
[Infinite-divisible-rank comparison]
\label{lem:infinite-divisible-bf}
Let $A,B$ be countable Abelian $p$-groups whose divisible ranks are
both infinite. Let $g:\langle\bar b\rangle\to\langle\bar a\rangle$
be the isomorphism induced by the indicated finite tuples.
The following conditions are sufficient for the displayed comparisons.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $\delta=\omega\gamma$,
$(A,\bar a)\le_{2\gamma+1}(B,\bar b)$ provided the Ulm
invariants agree below $\delta$ and, for $a=g(b)$, either
\[
 h_A(a)=h_B(b)<\delta,
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 h_B(b)\ge\delta,\qquad
 h_A(a)\ge\min\{h_B(b),\delta+\omega\}.
\]
\item $(A,\bar a)\le_{2\gamma+2}(B,\bar b)$ provided the
Ulm invariants agree below $\delta=\omega\gamma$,
\[
 u_B(\xi)\le u_A(\xi)
 \quad(\delta\le\xi<\delta+\omega),
\]
and each $a=g(b)$ either has the same height as $b$ below
$\delta+\omega$, or both heights are at least $\delta+\omega$.
\item At a nonzero limit $\eta$, $(A,\bar a)\le_\eta(B,\bar b)$
provided the Ulm invariants agree below $\omega\eta$ and heights
are equal below $\omega\eta$ and simultaneously above that cut.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: thm:no-pure-sigma
statements.statement_latex:
[No exact pure-$\Sigma$ complexity for any countable Abelian $p$-group]
\label{thm:no-pure-sigma}
No countable Abelian $p$-group has exact pure
$\Sigma_\alpha$ Scott complexity at any countable index.

statements.label: thm:finite-bare-hardness
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite depth-two obstruction]
\label{thm:finite-bare-hardness}
For either $\triangleleft\in\{<,\le\}$, consider pairs $(A,B)$ in the
finite fragment $\mathcal F_d$, with $d$ allowed to vary, satisfying
\[
 \forall\chi\text{ admissible in Definition~2.7 of \cite{WW}},\qquad
 \operatorname{val}(A\chi)\mathrel{\triangleleft}
 \operatorname{val}(B\chi)
\]
is $\Pi^0_1$-complete already when the terms use only $1$, independently
named ground-type variables, $+$ and $\E$, and have $\E$-nesting depth
at most two. Every value is a positive integer, and each output term
belongs to every $\C_i$, $i\ge1$. The same restricted completeness
holds for comparison of their norms.

statements.label: lem:seven-equations
statements.statement_latex:
[Seven-equation definition of multiplication]
\label{lem:seven-equations}
For positive $x,y,w$, put $a=x+y+1$ and $b=a+x$, treating these as
affine term abbreviations. Then $w=xy$ if and only if the following
seven source equations have a solution in positive integers
$s,t,u,v,q,r,h,k$:
\begin{align*}
 \E(a,u)+1&=u+\E(s,1),&
 \E(b,v)+1&=v+\E(t,1),\\
 \E(a,q)+y+1&=u+q+\E(a,1),&
 \E(b,r)+y+1&=v+r+\E(b,1),\\
 s+a+h&=\E(a,a),&
 t+b+k&=\E(b,b),\\
 t&=s+w.&&
\end{align*}
Every side has $\E$-nesting depth at most one.

statements.label: thm:bounded-bare-vectors
statements.statement_latex:
[Two-component bounded-vector obstruction]
\label{thm:bounded-bare-vectors}
Both strict and weak comparison in Definition~2.8 are undecidable even
on a computably constructed family of two-component $\C$-vectors whose
bounded norm is proved uniformly. The family gives $\Pi^0_1$-hardness
while retaining the finite depth-two terms as higher components.

statements.label: lem:normalization
statements.statement_latex:
[Effective normalization]\label{lem:normalization}
Every term in $\mathcal F_d$ has an effectively computable normal form
$\operatorname{nf}(f)$ of the shape \eqref{eq:normal-form}, with the same value
at every positive integer tuple.  All operations terminate by finite
syntax recursion.

statements.label: lem:ray
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite-family ray separation]\label{lem:ray}
Given a finite collection $\mathcal S$ of normal forms, close it under
taking keys and add zero.  One can effectively choose positive integers
$a_1,\ldots,a_d$ such that, on the ray $x_i=a_it$ with integer $t>0$,
the following statements hold for all $F,G\in\mathcal S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $F\ne G$, their difference is eventually nonzero with a fixed
      sign.
\item If $F,G$ are constant-free and distinct, then
      $|F(\mathbf a t)-G(\mathbf a t)|\ge t$ for all sufficiently large
      $t$.
\end{enumerate}
The common thresholds and the eventual signs are computable.

statements.label: thm:identity
statements.statement_latex:
[Decidable extensional equality]\label{thm:identity}
For any finite number of independent positive ground variables and any
finite exponential nesting depths,
\[
  (\forall\mathbf n>0)\ f(\mathbf n)=g(\mathbf n)
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \operatorname{nf}(f)=\operatorname{nf}(g).                 \tag{N4}
\]
Consequently extensional equality in $\mathcal F_d$ is decidable,
uniformly in $d$ and the two input terms.  If the normal forms differ,
a separating positive integer tuple can be computed.

statements.label: thm:unary
statements.statement_latex:
[One-variable universal comparison]\label{thm:unary}
Let $f,g\in\mathcal F_1$.  Both
\[
                 (\forall n>0)\ f(n)<g(n),\qquad
                 (\forall n>0)\ f(n)\le g(n)                \tag{N5}
\]
are decidable, uniformly at arbitrary finite exponential depth.
A false instance has an effectively computable least positive
counterexample.

statements.label: cor:consumers
statements.statement_latex:
[Further exact consumers]\label{cor:consumers}
The same procedures decide equality of finite-valued ordinal vectors
over any finite set of independent ground variables, and strict/weak
vector comparison and bounded norm for finite-valued $\mathcal O$-vectors
with one independent ground variable.  They also decide comparison
after any fixed affine one-parameter substitution with nonnegative
integer coefficients and positive coordinate values for finitely many
ground variables: explicitly,
$x_i=a_i n+b_i$ with $a_i,b_i\in\mathbb N$ and $a_i+b_i>0$.

statements.label: lem:bridge
statements.statement_latex:
\label{lem:bridge}
The comparability graphs of finite order forests are precisely
$\Forb(P_4,C_4)$. Each such graph determines its order forest up to
isomorphism. Moreover, for finite order forests $S,T$,
\[
 S\hookrightarrow T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Comp(S)\hookrightarrow\Comp(T).
\]

statements.label: thm:decision
statements.statement_latex:
\label{thm:decision}
There is an algorithm which, given any finite family $\mathcal U$ of
finite order forests, decides whether $\mathcal C(\mathcal U)$ has JEP.
More precisely, set
\[
 \mathcal F=\{P_4,C_4\}\cup\{\Comp(U):U\in\mathcal U\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal C(\mathcal U)$ has JEP if and only if $\Forb(\mathcal F)$
has JEP.

statements.label: prop:certificate
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite certificates for negative instances]
\label{prop:certificate}
If $\mathcal C(\mathcal U)$ fails JEP, one can compute a pair $F,G$ in
the class and a finite exhaustive certificate that they have no common
extension in the class.

statements.label: thm:width
prop:age
statements.statement_latex:
\label{prop:age}
A nonempty hereditary class $\mathcal K$ of finite forests is the age
of a finite or countable forest if and only if it has JEP. If it contains
forests of unbounded size, the realizing forest is countably infinite.

statements.label: prop:counter-bound
statements.statement_latex:
[Countervaluation bounds]\label{prop:counter-bound}
The fixed-control comparison problem is co-recursively-enumerable.  It is
decidable if and only if there is a total computable function $b(Q)$ such
that each false comparison $Q$ has a countervaluation whose every coordinate
is at most $b(Q)$.

statements.label: lem:finite-balls
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite norm balls]\label{lem:finite-balls}
Each norm ball is finite and can be effectively enumerated.  Cantor-normal-form
comparison, natural sum and natural product are effective.  Moreover
$\norm(\alpha\oplus\beta)=\norm(\alpha)+\norm(\beta)$.

statements.label: lem:phi-growth
statements.statement_latex:
[Elementary control properties]\label{lem:phi-growth}
The fixed $\Phi$ is computable, strictly increasing, and greater than the
identity.  On its whole domain,
\[
 \Phi(t+1)\ge 2^{\,2^{\Phi(t)}}.
\]
In particular $\Phi(t+1)>4\Phi(t)+4$.

statements.label: lem:controlled-strictness
statements.statement_latex:
[Controlled strictness and finite values]\label{lem:controlled-strictness}
If $\beta<\alpha$ and
$\norm(\beta)\le\Phi(\norm(\alpha))$, then
$\psi(\beta)+1\le\psi(\alpha)$.  Also $\psi(n)=n$ for finite $n$.

statements.label: thm:maximum
statements.statement_latex:
[Effective maximum predecessor]\label{thm:maximum}
The following simultaneous recursion computes $M$ and $L$ exactly.
Write $\alpha=\omega^e c+r$ with $c>0$ and $r<\omega^e$, and put
$w=1+\norm(e)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M(\alpha,0)=0$ and $L(0,b)=L(e,0)=0$.
\item If $r>0$ and $cw\le b$, retain the leading block:
 $M(\alpha,b)=\omega^e c+M(r,b-cw)$.
\item Otherwise set $d=\min(c-1,\lfloor b/w\rfloor)$ when $r=0$,
 and $d=\min(c,\lfloor b/w\rfloor)$ when $r>0$.  Then
 $M(\alpha,b)=\omega^e d+L(e,b-dw)$, omitting a zero block.
\item For $e,b>0$, let $a=M(e,b-1)$, $v=1+\norm(a)$ and
 $(q,s)=\operatorname{divmod}(b,v)$.  Then
 $L(e,b)=\omega^a q+L(a,s)$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: lem:saturation
thm:single-predecessor
statements.statement_latex:
[Single-predecessor recurrence]\label{thm:single-predecessor}
For every nonzero limit $\lambda<\varepsilon_0$ and $n\in\N$,
\[
 \psi(\lambda+n)=
 \psi\bigl(M(\lambda,\Phi(\norm(\lambda)+n))\bigr)+1.
\]

statements.label: cor:closed-evaluation
statements.statement_latex:
[Closed evaluation]\label{cor:closed-evaluation}
Every supplied closed collapse value is computable.  At a nonfinite state
$\alpha=\lambda+n$, replace $\alpha$ by
$M(\lambda,\Phi(\norm(\alpha)))$ and increment a counter.  On reaching
a finite state return that state plus the counter.

statements.label: thm:complete-count
statements.statement_latex:
[Complete terminal decomposition]\label{thm:complete-count}
Put $\nu=\norm(\lambda)$ and let $t\ge\nu$ be the total initial norm.
Starting at $\lambda+(t-\nu)$, let $\tau_\lambda(t)$ be the number of
nonfinite replacements and $Z_\lambda(t)$ the first finite state.  Then
\[
 J_\lambda(t):=\psi(\lambda+t-\nu)
       =Z_\lambda(t)+\tau_\lambda(t),\qquad
 Z_\lambda(t)=\Phi^{\tau_\lambda(t)}(t).
\]
The count is positive.  In particular $Z_\lambda(t)<J_\lambda(t)<2Z_\lambda(t)$.

statements.label: cor:finite-head
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite coefficient identity]\label{cor:finite-head}
For finite $k,n$,
\[
 \psi(\omega k+n)=\Phi^k(2k+n)+k.
\]

statements.label: lem:tail-separation
statements.statement_latex:
[Strict separation in one finite tail]\label{lem:tail-separation}
For $h_\lambda(n)=\psi(\lambda+n)$ with a fixed nonzero limit $\lambda$,
\[
 h_\lambda(n+1)>2^{h_\lambda(n)}.
\]
In particular every such function is injective.

statements.label: thm:forward-translation
statements.statement_latex:
[Actual-source forward translation]\label{thm:forward-translation}
For a literal original source with only ground free names, all positive
canonical coordinates are closed and effectively evaluable.  Coordinate
zero is effectively a finite expression in positive-natural inputs, constants,
addition and fixed functions $h_\lambda(n)=\psi(\lambda+n)$, where each
direct index is $\lambda=\omega\otimes c>0$ for a closed $c$.
The translation preserves every shared input valuation, including arbitrary
internal types, binders and recursors.

statements.label: cor:source-classes
statements.statement_latex:
[Two natural positive classes]\label{cor:source-classes}
In a recursor-free source every positive coordinate is finite.  If every
internal type and subtype has level at most two, every direct scalar index
is a polynomial limit below $\omega^\omega$.

statements.label: lem:sparse
statements.statement_latex:
[Sparse peaks]\label{lem:sparse}
For an infinite input of norm $t\ge2$, write $Z=f^L(t)=f(s)$ as in (1.3).
Then $0<L\le s-1$, and
\[
           Z<\psi(\alpha)=Z+L<2Z<f(s+1).             \tag{1.6}
\]
Distinct peaks $f(s)$ and $f(u)$ with $u<s$ satisfy $f(u)\le f(s-1)$.

statements.label: lem:roots
statements.statement_latex:
[Orbit cancellation at roots]\label{lem:roots}
Call a natural number an $f$-root if it is outside $\operatorname{range}(f)$.
If infinite inputs $\alpha,\beta$ have root norms $t,u$ and equal peaks,
then $\alpha=\beta$.

statements.label: thm:identity
statements.statement_latex:
[Identity normal form]\label{thm:identity}
For $E,F\in\mathcal P_d$, the identity $E=F$ holds at every positive
valuation exactly when $\NF(E)=\NF(F)$. If the forms differ, one can
effectively specify a positive countervaluation of the form
\[
           x_i=w_i(f(k)+1),\qquad w_i,k\in\NN.        \tag{2.2}
\]
Consequently universal equality in $\mathcal P_d$ is decidable.

statements.label: lem:oneinput
statements.statement_latex:
[Common-band or root separation]\label{lem:oneinput}
For any finite collection of normal forms in $\mathcal P_1$, a computable
$N$ has the following properties for every $x\ge N$.
Every affine open atom input lies in $[x,f(x))$. Every nonlinear atom input
is a root strictly greater than $f(x)$. Equal peaks of two tags force equal
indices and equal argument values.

statements.label: thm:zeros
statements.statement_latex:
[Effective finite zeros]\label{thm:zeros}
Given $E,F\in\mathcal P_1$, one computes $N\ge1$ such that either their
normal forms agree, or $E(x)\ne F(x)$ for every $x\ge N$. In the latter
case their equality set is the computable finite set obtained by exact
evaluation at $1,\ldots,N-1$.

statements.label: lem:cells
statements.statement_latex:
[Range cells and signed rows]\label{lem:cells}
The following assertions have effective tail bounds.
For a nonlinear positive expression $E$, let $Z_i$ be its displayed open
tag peaks, and $Y=\max_i Z_i=f(s)$. Then
\[
              Y<E<f(s+1),\qquad E<h_\omega(Y).        \tag{3.1}
\]
For a value $V\in\operatorname{range}(f)$ on that tail,
\[
 V<E\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (\exists i\ Z_i\ge V),\qquad
 V>E\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (\forall i\ Z_i<V).       \tag{3.2}
\]
After cancellation of identical tags in a signed row, its eventual
pointwise sign is the coefficient sign of its greatest remaining peak,
once those peaks have been ordered. If no tags remain, the row is affine.

statements.label: lem:prefix
statements.statement_latex:
[Exact prefix splitting]\label{lem:prefix}
Let $\kappa$ be a fixed Cantor prefix and let $\eta$ be a nonzero limit
whose leading monomial is at most the least monomial of $\kappa$;
the zero prefix is also allowed. In particular one may take
$\kappa=\pi k$ and $\operatorname{lead}(\eta)\le\pi$.
For $b\ge c=\norm(\kappa)$,
\[
 M(\kappa+\eta,b)=\kappa+M(\eta,b-c).                \tag{4.2}
\]
A descent above $\kappa$ reaches a state $\kappa+n$ with finite remainder
before passing below $\kappa$. During that segment the remainder's exact
norm control is
\[
                   G_c(v)=f(c+v)-c\ge f(v)>v.         \tag{4.3}
\]

statements.label: lem:counts
statements.statement_latex:
[Ordered controls and counts]\label{lem:counts}
For increasing integer controls $g\le h$, both strictly exceeding their
input, let $L_g,L_h$ be the respective norm-maximal descent counts.
Then
\[
 \alpha\le\beta,quad\norm(\alpha)\le\norm(\beta)
       \quad\Longrightarrow\quad L_g(\alpha)\le L_h(\beta). \tag{4.4}
\]

statements.label: lem:peakword
statements.statement_latex:
[Exact peak word]\label{lem:peakword}
For each fixed limit $\lambda$, one computes a finite word $W_\lambda$ of
principal kernels such that the peak of $h_\lambda(A)$ is exactly
\[
             Z_{\lambda,A}=W_\lambda(\norm(\lambda)+A). \tag{4.5}
\]
The omitted count is positive: $h_\lambda(A)=Z_{\lambda,A}+D_{\lambda,A}$.

statements.label: lem:stage
statements.statement_latex:
[One-stage reserve consumer]\label{lem:stage}
Let $\rho<\pi m$ be a fixed nonzero limit, $m\ge1$, and begin an ordinary
descent at $A=\pi(k+m)+n$, of norm $X\ge x\ge\norm(\rho)$.
At its first cut $\pi k+n'$ with finite remainder,
\[
        n'>J_\rho(x):=f^{D_\rho(x)}(x)+D_\rho(x),    \tag{5.1}
\]
where $D_\rho(x)$ is the count from
$\rho+(x-\norm(\rho))$.

statements.label: lem:reserve
statements.statement_latex:
[Effective profile reserve]\label{lem:reserve}
From a lower profile $P$ below $L>\omega$ one computes a nonempty word
\[
 F=h_{\rho_l}\circ\cdots\circ h_{\rho_1},\quad
 F(z)>P(z)\ (z\ge z_0),\quad
 R=\sum_j(\norm(\rho_j)+1),\quad
 H=\max_j\norm(\operatorname{lead}(\rho_j)),          \tag{5.2}
\]
with every $\rho_j<L$. If $\pi\ge\omega$ is principal and at least every
displayed leading monomial, a descent from $\pi R+n$, $n\ge z\ge z_0$,
has terminal norm greater than $P(z)$. The same conclusion holds with any
additional permanent numerical mass $c$.

statements.label: lem:direct
statements.statement_latex:
[Direct kernel growth]\label{lem:direct}
For fixed $L>\omega$ principal and fixed lower profile $P$, one computes
$T$ such that, for $t\ge T$ and every genuine mass $0\le c\le t-\norm(L)$,
\[
                         \KK Lc(t)>P(t).             \tag{5.3}
\]
Also, $\KK\pi c(t)\le h_\pi(t)$ on its genuine domain.

statements.label: thm:adjacent
statements.statement_latex:
[Cross-mass strict-input separation]\label{thm:adjacent}
For a fixed principal $L>\omega$ and fixed lower profile $P$ with reserve
data (5.2), put
\[
              T=\max(4,R+5,z_0,\norm L,H).            \tag{6.1}
\]
For $t\ge T$, $0\le c\le t+1-\norm L$, and
$0\le e\le t-\norm L$,
\[
       \KK Lc(t+1)>P(\KK Le(t)+\EE Le(t)).            \tag{6.2}
\]
There is no ordering requirement on $c,e$. More generally the same
conclusion holds with any $u>t$ and any mass genuine at $u$ on the left.

statements.label: thm:limitmass
statements.statement_latex:
[Limit-exponent mass separation]\label{thm:limitmass}
Let $L=\omega^\beta$ with $\beta$ a nonzero limit. For a fixed lower
profile $P$ and data (5.2), put
\[
           T=\max(4,R+4,z_0,\norm L+1,H).            \tag{6.5}
\]
For $t\ge T$ and $0\le c<e\le t-\norm L$,
\[
                \KK Lc(t)>P(\KK Le(t)+\EE Le(t)).    \tag{6.6}
\]
Consequently the lexicographically larger pair $(\text{input},-\text{mass})$
gives domination against every fixed lower profile, on an effective
genuine tail. Equal pairs give equal values.

statements.label: lem:successor
lem:small
statements.statement_latex:
[Small principal kernels]\label{lem:small}
On their genuine domains,
\[
 \KK\omega c(t)=f(t),\quad\EE\omega c(t)=1,\qquad
 \EE{\omega^2}c(t)=f(t)/2-\lceil c/2\rceil+1.         \tag{7.4}
\]
Thus $\omega^2$ kernels at the same input have exactly the mass classes
$\lceil c/2\rceil$, ordered in reverse. The control has even values.

statements.label: thm:mass
statements.statement_latex:
[Strict mass order above degree two]\label{thm:mass}
For every fixed principal $L\ge\omega^3$, a computable $T_L$ satisfies
\[
 t\ge T_L,quad0\le c<e\le t-\norm L
                 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad\KK Lc(t)>\KK Le(t). \tag{7.5}
\]
For a nonzero limit exponent take $T_L=\max(7,\norm L+1)$.
For $L=\theta\omega$, $\theta\ge\omega^2$, $w=\norm\theta$, take
\[
 T_L=\max(4,\norm L,2w,\max(8,w),S_\theta),          \tag{7.6}
\]
where $S_\theta=0$ at $\theta=\omega^2$ and otherwise $S_\theta=T_\theta$.

statements.label: thm:sign
statements.statement_latex:
[Effective eventual signs]\label{thm:sign}
Given two expressions in these sorts, one computes a sign
$\sigma\in\{-1,0,1\}$ and $N\ge1$ such that their difference has sign
$\sigma$ for every $x\ge N$. In particular this holds for every pair in
$\mathcal P_1$.

statements.label: cor:boolean
statements.statement_latex:
[One-input quantified comparison]\label{cor:boolean}
For any finite Boolean combination of equality, weak-order and strict-order
atoms between expressions of $\mathcal P_1$, each of its existential and
universal closures over $x\in\NN$ is decidable.

statements.label: cor:sourceeq

statements.statement_latex:
[Whole one-ground-name source comparison]
Every finite Boolean combination of these pointwise vector equality,
weak-comparison and strict-comparison atoms is decidable under one
existential or universal quantifier over its shared positive ground
coordinate. Arbitrary original internal types and output levels are allowed.

statements.label: lem:growth
statements.statement_latex:
[Growth]\label{lem:growth}
Each $F_j$ is recursive and strictly increasing, with $F_j(n)\ge2^n$.
For $j\ge0$,
\[
 F_{j+1}(n+1)\ge2^{F_{j+1}(n)+1}.
\]
Consequently $f(z+1)\ge(A+2)f(z)$ whenever $z\ge A\ge0$.

statements.label: lem:residues
statements.statement_latex:
[Effective constant residues]\label{lem:residues}
For every $m\ge1$ one can compute $r_m\in[0,m)$ such that
\[
 F_j(n)\equiv r_m\pmod m\quad(j\ge1,\ n\ge m).
\]
In particular $f(n)\equiv r_m\pmod m$ for $n\ge\max(0,m-100)$.
For $s\ge1$, $j\ge2$, this can be strengthened to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:envelope}
 m\le 2^{2^s}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F_j(s)\equiv r_m\pmod m.
\end{equation}
If $B=f(u)$ and $m\le2^{2^B}$, then also $f(u+1)\equiv r_m\pmod m$.

statements.label: thm:snyatkov
thm:finite-source
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite-coefficient source comparison]\label{thm:finite-source}
Take two original well-typed $T$ terms of the same type with ground free
variables. Compute their canonical assignments. Suppose that at every
zeroth-coordinate collapse $\psi(\omega\otimes c+g)$ its closed coefficient
$c$ has finite ordinal value. Their universal weak, WW-strict, and equality
comparisons are decidable. Every recursor-free such term passes this test,
with no bound on its internal types.

statements.label: lem:kernel-recursion
lem:uniform
statements.statement_latex:
[Uniform kernel separation]\label{lem:uniform}
Put $C_d=1000d^2$, $T_3=16$, and for $d\ge4$ put
$T_d=\max(T_{d-1},100C_{d-1}+100d)$. For $d\ge3$, $c,e\ge0$, signed
$j,k$, and $R\ge0$, suppose
\begin{equation}\label{eq:region}
 t\ge T_d,\qquad
 f(t)\ge C_d(c+e+|j|+|k|+R+1).
\end{equation}
Then the depths are defined and at least $f(t)$, and
\begin{align*}
 X^d_{c,j}(t+1)&>f^R(X^d_{e,k}(t)),\\
 c<e\quad&\Longrightarrow\quad
 X^d_{c,j}(t)>f^R(X^d_{e,k}(t)).
\end{align*}
At equal input and equal $c$, exact order is order of $j$. On a common
computed tail, equality of two rank-$d$ values occurs exactly when input,
$c$, and $j$ are identical.

statements.label: lem:counter
lem:kernel-residues
lem:guards
statements.statement_latex:
[Ordered maximum-variable guards]\label{lem:guards}
For two words $A(x),B(y)$ and the guard $x\ge y$, an effective common
tail permits their three-way comparison to be rewritten as a finite Boolean
combination in which $x$ occurs only linearly and words are applied only
to the remaining variable $y$. For two words at the \emph{same} raw
variable the corresponding tail comparison is effectively decided.
All thresholds and newly generated words are computed before the tail is
used.

statements.label: lem:row
statements.statement_latex:
[Ranked cancellation]\label{lem:row}
For a finite collection of word-linear rows and a chosen maximal raw
variable $x$, one can compute a tail and finite guarded cases in which
each row either has a known strict sign or is exactly linear in $x$.
The guards can themselves be made linear in $x$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:guards}. No correlation between word values is discarded.

statements.label: thm:existential
statements.statement_latex:
[Closed existential word arithmetic]\label{thm:existential}
The existential closure of every Boolean combination of word-linear row
comparisons and fixed-modulus congruences in the finite-degree language
above is decidable, on its explicit word domains.

statements.label: thm:graphs
statements.statement_latex:
[Polynomial collapse graphs]\label{thm:graphs}
For each fixed nonzero polynomial limit $\lambda<\omega^\omega$, the graph
$y=h_\lambda(n)$ is effectively expressible as a finite disjunction of
word-linear equations in $n,y$, with explicit domains and exact finite
exceptions. One finite degree bound suffices for each finite collection of
such graphs. Arbitrary fixed nesting and addition of these functions admit
a total functional existential graph translation.

statements.label: thm:leveltwo
statements.statement_latex:
[Canonical source comparison through level two]\label{thm:leveltwo}
Universal weak, WW-strict, and equality comparison is decidable for original
canonical $T$ assignments with ground free variables and maximum internal
type level at most two. The maximum includes every subterm and binder type,
not merely the result and free-variable types.

statements.label: lem:endpoints
thm:common
statements.statement_latex:
[Common-head layers]\label{thm:common}
For $E,F\in\mathcal A_r$, each pointwise relation $E<F$, $E=F$, $E>F$
has an effectively constructed formula in $(\N;0,1,+,<,f)$ with the same
raw free variables and exactly the same truth at every positive valuation.
Hence arbitrary Boolean and quantified combinations of certified comparisons
are decidable.

statements.label: lem:head-window
statements.statement_latex:
[Head order in a strict interval]\label{lem:head-window}
Let $\lambda>\mu$ be nonzero fixed limits. If
$t\ge\max(N(\lambda),N(\mu)+2)$ and
$N(\mu)\le u<f(t)$, then $J_\lambda(t)>J_\mu(u)$ and their endpoints
differ. Consequently, if finitely many norm inputs $t_i$ have minimum
$s\ge\max_iN(\lambda_i)+2$ and $\max_i t_i<f(s)$, their outputs are
ordered lexicographically by (ordinal head, norm input). Equality requires
equality of both, and different output blocks have distinct sparse endpoints.

statements.label: thm:balanced
statements.statement_latex:
[Balanced comparison]\label{thm:balanced}
For two expressions with one finite balanced certificate, their three-way
pointwise comparison has an effectively constructed base formula in
$(\N;0,1,+,<,f)$ with exactly the same free variables. Arbitrary Boolean
and quantified combinations of such comparisons are decidable.

statements.label: thm:single-core
statements.statement_latex:
[Arbitrary single-core rows]\label{thm:single-core}
For the signed row
\begin{equation}\label{eq:single-core}
 Q(\vec x)=K+rE(\vec x)+
       \sum_i q_i h_{\lambda_i}(a_iE(\vec x)+c_i),
 \quad a_i\ge1,\ c_i\ge0,
\end{equation}
with fixed integer $K,r,q_i$ and fixed nonzero limit heads, each sign
predicate $Q<0$, $Q=0$, $Q>0$ has an effectively computable finite
Presburger formula in the original raw variables. Thus universal comparison
of these rows needs no arithmetic decision theorem about $f$.

statements.label: lem:addition
statements.statement_latex:
[Addition and small constants]\label{lem:addition}
Natural addition $n_a+n_b=n_c$ is defined by the two source equations
\[
 e(b,0)=e(0,d),\qquad e(a,d)=e(c,0),
\]
with one fresh positive raw witness $d$.  Arithmetic one has a constant-size
source-equation definition.  Every binary literal $k$ has an addition DAG
of size $O(\log(k+1))$ once zero and one are available.

statements.label: lem:sort
statements.statement_latex:
[Superincreasing pair coding]\label{lem:sort}
Let $q(n)=F_S(n)=\Phi(n+4)$.  Then
\[
 q(a)+q(b)=q(c)+q(d)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\{a,b\}=\{c,d\}
\]
as multisets.  Consequently sorting two naturals has a primitive-positive
definition using addition and the actual $S$ graph.

statements.label: lem:collision
statements.statement_latex:
[Six-eraser collision detector]\label{lem:collision}
For arbitrary actual ground sources $P,Q$, put
\[
 L=e(e(P,P),e(Q,Q)),\qquad R=e(e(P,Q),e(Q,P)).
\]
At every joint valuation $L_0\ge R_0$, with equality exactly when
$P_0=Q_0$.  Otherwise $L_0-R_0\ge2$.

statements.label: lem:aggregate
statements.statement_latex:
[Conjunction without cancellation]\label{lem:aggregate}
A finite conjunction of actual ground-source equations can be transformed
into ground sources $L,R$ with $L_0\ge R_0$ everywhere, equality precisely
when every equation holds, and otherwise gap at least two.

statements.label: thm:compiler
statements.statement_latex:
[One unconditional comparison]\label{thm:compiler}
Every existential $\Esrc$ sentence has a computably constructed ground-output
strict comparison, and one weak comparison, true precisely when the sentence
is false.  All free variables of the resulting sources are ground.  Shared
inputs and source leaves retain their valuations.  The added source DAG size
is polynomial in the formula DAG, binary constants and supplied source DAGs.

statements.label: cor:ground-equivalence
lem:absolute
statements.statement_latex:
[Absolute observer]\label{lem:absolute}
Let $T:\rho$ have only ground free names $\mathbf z$.  Its entire raw scalar
graph $v=\can{T(\mathbf z)}_0$ is existentially definable by actual ground-source
observations, addition and constants, with all shared names preserved.

statements.label: thm:decision-equivalence
statements.statement_latex:
[Exact decision equivalence]\label{thm:decision-equivalence}
Universal weak/strict canonical comparison on the full all-ground-free-variable
domain, its ground-output restriction, and unsatisfiability in $\Esrc$ are
computably equivalent.  Satisfiability uses answer complementation.

statements.label: lem:one-unit
statements.statement_latex:
[One-name scalar elimination]\label{lem:one-unit}
Let $A:\tau$ be an actual source, $h=\can A$, $m=\lv(\tau)$, and let
$X:\sigma$ be one of its free functional names.  Put
\[
 n=\lv(\sigma)+1,\quad d=2^n\sum_{i=0}^m\sz^X(h_i),\quad
 P=(\partial^X_0h_0)_0,\quad R=h_0\{X:=\mathbf1\},\quad L=\lambda X.A.
\]
The graph of the desired scalar $R$ has a finite positive-coefficient linear
definition using scalar observations of actual sources without free $X$.

statements.label: thm:unit-elimination
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite unit-observation elimination]\label{thm:unit-elimination}
For an actual source $A$ and a finite set of all its free functional names,
the absolute scalar after their common unit observation is existentially
definable in $\Esrc$, retaining all original shared ground inputs.

statements.label: lem:affine-head
statements.statement_latex:
[Affine heads and their finite surplus]\label{lem:affine-head}
Every functional context has an additive first-field tree with leaves $F_1$
and whole $F$-free positive expressions.  At a selected collapse with head
$h$, its tail is $F$-active whenever $h$ is active.  At common units there is
a finite $\delta(h)\ge0$ such that
\[
 (\partial^F_1h)_1=h^*+\delta(h).
\]
The surplus is zero only at the bare leaf $F_1$; a nonfinite $h^*$ has
$\delta(h)\ge1$.  The output-two head partial is finite.

statements.label: lem:carriers
statements.statement_latex:
[Actual unary carriers]\label{lem:carriers}
Each selected nonfinite head has an actual unary carrier with that exact
unit first field.  Its ground captures can be closed to zero without changing
the field, and its actual scalar is retained.

statements.label: lem:reserve
statements.statement_latex:
[Multiset accounting and ground transport]\label{lem:reserve}
For every annotated scalar $q$ there are an actual-carrier multiset
$\mathcal M(q)$ and a finite $c(q)\ge0$ with
\[
 (\partial^F_0q)_1=\sum_{V\in\mathcal M(q)}V_1+c(q),\qquad
 d(q)=c(q)-3|\mathcal M(q)|.
\]
On the generated active sources, $d\ge1$; it is at least four except
possibly at the bare functional source $F$.  Ground units preserve the
multiset and $d$, and a ground scalar partial preserves the multiset and
does not decrease $d$.

statements.label: lem:chain
statements.statement_latex:
[One final abstraction]\label{lem:chain}
For actual unary sources $V_j$ free of a fresh $x$,
\[
 \can{\lambda x.V_1(\cdots(V_mx)\cdots)}_1
       =\sum_{j=1}^m(V_{j,1}+3)+1.
\]

statements.label: thm:ground-construction
statements.statement_latex:
[Original-budget ground-binder construction]\label{thm:ground-construction}
Let $P:o$ be $F$-active in the complete grammar, $B=\lambda F.P$, and
let $C:\sigma_k$ be an actual $F$-free caller.  Write $b$ for the second
field of the original full box $\can B\square\can C$.
Then $b=B_2$ is finite, $b\ge4$, and at $\mathcal N=2^b$ one effectively
constructs an actual unit-open unary $K$ with
\[
 \mathcal N(B_1+C_1)=K_1+\Delta,\qquad \Delta\in\N,\quad\Delta>0.
\]
No child construction certificate or enlargement of the original scale is
assumed.

statements.label: thm:head-graph
statements.statement_latex:
[Whole-head graph from a paid certificate]\label{thm:head-graph}
Suppose actual sources $B,C,K$ and a finite original box $b$ supply
$a=2^b(B_1+C_1)=K_1+\Delta$ at common functional units, where
$\Delta\ge0$ is finite and $K:o\to o$ is unit open.  Then the complete
genuine graph of
\[
 J_\xi(t)=\psi(\xi+t-\norm(\xi)),\quad
 \xi=\omega\otimes a,\quad t\ge\norm(\xi),
\]
is effectively existentially definable in actual-source arithmetic.  It
retains the original scalar/input wires of $B,C$ and every finite-prefix input.

statements.label: lem:pair-compiler
statements.statement_latex:
[Signed polynomial pairs]\label{lem:pair-compiler}
Every signed linear expression $D$ in ordinal unknowns with coefficients
in $\mathbb Z[\omega]$ has effectively constructed actual $A_D,B_D:\tau$
whose first-coordinate difference is $2^kD$ for a finite $k$.
All free functional variables have type $\tau$, and internal types have
level at most two.  Differences are taken only in the signed Cantor-monomial
group; each of the two source coordinates remains a positive ordinal.

statements.label: lem:functional-detector
statements.statement_latex:
[Alignment and a full-vector detector]\label{lem:functional-detector}
The condition $\can A_1=\can B_1$ is equivalent to existence of two fresh
positive ground inputs making the full canonical vectors of
\[
 A'=(\lambda t:o.A)z,\qquad B'=(\lambda t:o.B)w
\]
equal.  Full-vector equality of any actual pair of type $\tau$ can in turn
be detected by ground sources $L,R$ satisfying $L_0\ge R_0$, with equality
exactly at vector equality and otherwise gap at least two.

statements.label: thm:functional-hardness
statements.statement_latex:
[Standard-control functional-input undecidability]
\label{thm:functional-hardness}
Full universal canonical weak comparison and strict comparison are
undecidable already for ground output, free-variable levels at most one,
and internal levels at most two.  The reduction at this level uses finitely
many comparison queries.  A computable single-query reduction from the
same polynomial-system unsatisfiability problem is available with internal
level at most three.

statements.label: lem:perturbed-control
statements.statement_latex:
[Control properties]\label{lem:perturbed-control}
The function $\Gamma_b$ is primitive recursive, agrees with $\Phi$ on
$[0,b]$, and satisfies
\[
 0\le\Gamma_b(n)-\Phi(n)\le1,\quad
 \Phi(n)\le\Gamma_b(n)<\Phi(n+1),\quad
 \Gamma_b(n+1)>4\Gamma_b(n).
\]
It has the additive margin
$\Gamma_b(v+a)\ge\Gamma_b(v)+2a$ for $a\ge1$, is eventually bounded
by $F_6$, and $\Gamma_b(n)/\Phi(n)\to1$.

statements.label: thm:control-hardness
statements.statement_latex:
[Ground hardness within distance one]\label{thm:control-hardness}
For every $b$, universal canonical weak comparison and strict comparison
at the one fixed control $\Gamma_b$ are $\Pi^0_1$-complete already on
ground-output sources having only ground free names and ground binders,
using only the prime constants $0,S$, with internal levels at most one.
Moreover $\Gamma_b(n)\bmod2$ is not eventually periodic.

statements.label: prop:complete
statements.statement_latex:
[Complete-count identity]\label{prop:complete}
The descent terminates and
\[
 Z_\lambda(t)=f^{\,\tau_\lambda(t)}(t),\qquad
 J_\lambda(t)=Z_\lambda(t)+\tau_\lambda(t).
\]

statements.label: thm:envelope
lem:fixed
statements.statement_latex:
[A fixed-budget count]\label{lem:fixed}
Fix a nonnegative retained mass $c$ and take $S\ge c+d+1$.
Start the suffix at $\omega^d$ with any finite tail of total norm
(including $c$) at most $S$. At every replacement spend the constant
suffix budget $S-c$ and stop when the suffix is finite. The number of
replacements is $p_d(S-c)$. When $c=\norm(\pi)$ for a retained
CNF prefix $\pi$ of least exponent at least $d$, this is precisely
the corresponding segment starting at $\pi+\omega^d$ plus that tail.

statements.label: lem:period
statements.statement_latex:
[A sufficient partition period]\label{lem:period}
For every $d,m\ge1$, put $Q_d=d!m^{d-1}$. Then
\[
             p_d(n+Q_d)\equiv p_d(n)\pmod m\quad(n\ge0).
\]

statements.label: thm:transfer
statements.statement_latex:
[Congruent-budget transfer]\label{thm:transfer}
Consider deletion of one suffix block $\omega^d$, with retained
numerical mass $c\ge0$ and initial total norm at least $c+d+1$,
under budgets at least the current total norm. Suppose
every budget used in this segment is congruent to one integer $S$
modulo $Q_d=d!m^{d-1}$, where $S\ge c$. Then its complete segment
count is congruent to $p_d(S-c)$ modulo $m$.

statements.label: prop:omega-block
statements.statement_latex:
[An actual $\omega^\omega$ block]\label{prop:omega-block}
Let $\Omega=\omega^\omega$. At a real suffix state $\pi+\Omega+n$, with $\pi$ a retained CNF
prefix (zero or of least exponent at least $\omega$), and total norm $u$,
assume $c=\norm(\pi)$, $c+3\le u$, and
$B=f(u)\ge\max(16,m)$. Put $C=f(u+1)$ and $d=B-c-1$.
If $H_c(u)$ counts the complete deletion of this $\Omega$ copy,
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:omega-block}
 H_c(u)\equiv1+p_{B-c-1}(C-c)\pmod m.
\end{equation}
Its output norm is still exactly $f^{H_c(u)}(u)$.

statements.label: lem:entry
statements.statement_latex:
[The retained prefix at first entry]\label{lem:entry}
The predecessor of this $\Theta$ state is
\[
 \Omega q+1,\qquad q=(u-1)/3.
\]
The first $\Omega$ copy deleted in this polynomial has retained
prefix norm $e=u-4$ and total input norm $u$.

statements.label: lem:matrix
statements.statement_latex:
[Exact state update]\label{lem:matrix}
For $U\in V_d$,
\[
 \Lambda_b(U/A_d)=\frac{\Lambda_b(UA_d)}{A_d}.
\]
The updated numerator is again in $V_d$. In the coefficient basis its
matrix is
$T_b[i,j]=[z^{2i+b-j}]A_d$, for $0\le i,j<D$.

statements.label: thm:observer
statements.statement_latex:
[Complete selected coefficient]\label{thm:observer}
If $n=\sum_{i<L}b_i2^i$, with bits read least significant first,
then
\[
 p_d(n)\bmod2=e_0^{T}T_{b_{L-1}}\cdots T_{b_0}e_0.
\]

statements.label: lem:observable
statements.statement_latex:
[All-continuation observability]\label{lem:observable}
For any field $K$, polynomial $A$ with $A(0)=1$ and $\deg A=D$,
the first $D$ coefficients of $U/A$ determine every $U$ of degree
less than $D$. For the binary observer above, distinct numerator
states are distinguished by some continuation of length at most
$\lceil\log_2 D\rceil$.

statements.label: lem:local
statements.statement_latex:
[Local rule]\label{lem:local}
For a fixed pole $\zeta$ and $b\in K$,
\[
 \mathcal C\!\left(\frac{b\,dz}{(z-\zeta)^{2j}}\right)=0,\qquad
 \mathcal C\!\left(\frac{b\,dz}{(z-\zeta)^{2j+1}}\right)
       =\frac{b^{1/2}\,dz}{(z-\zeta)^{j+1}}.
\]
The same definition gives
$\mathcal C(\sum a_nz^n\,dz)=\sum a_{2n+1}^{1/2}z^n\,dz$.

statements.label: lem:poles
statements.statement_latex:
[Removal of every higher pole]\label{lem:poles}
Put $\mu=\sum_{i=1}^d2^{\nu_2(i)}$ and
$a=\lceil\log_2\mu\rceil$. After $a$ Cartier applications to
a proper differential with denominator $A_d$, all surviving finite
poles are simple. Its simple residues subsequently undergo inverse
Frobenius at their fixed poles. No polynomial part is created.

statements.label: lem:residue
statements.statement_latex:
[The actual residue formula]\label{lem:residue}
The form $\omega_e=z^{e-1}A_d(z)^{-1}\,dz$ has a simple nonzero
residue at each primitive $q$-th root $\zeta$, given by
\[
 b_\zeta=\frac{\zeta^e}{A_{d-q}(\zeta)}
                 =\zeta^{e-\Delta}A_{m_0}(\zeta).
\]

statements.label: lem:bounds
statements.statement_latex:
[The bounds needed for the root count]\label{lem:bounds}
For the actual linked inputs, $r\ge96$, $\Delta<r$, and
\[
 0<\Delta-2e<q,\qquad
 \varphi(q)>\frac{2^r}{r+1}>2^{2r/3}\Delta.
\]

statements.label: thm:actual-period
statements.statement_latex:
[Exact actual residue-tuple period]\label{thm:actual-period}
The tuple $(b_\zeta)_{\zeta\ {\rm primitive}\ q}$ has exact
Frobenius period $2r$. Every eventual period of the complete
rational differential Cartier orbit of $\omega_e$ is divisible
by $2r=2(\log_2 B-1)$.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.statement_latex:
[Universal properness]\label{thm:main}
Let $p$ be an additive idempotent ultrafilter on all subsets of $\R$
such that $(0,\epsilon)\in p$ for every $\epsilon>0$. There is a function
$f:\R\to(0,1]$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\eta>0$, $\{x:f(x)<\eta\}\in p$.
\item For every $g:\R\to\R$ with $\{x:g(x)=f(x)\}\in p$, there is a set
      $S_g\in p$ at every point of which $g$ is discontinuous.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently $[f]_p$ is a positive infinitesimal outside $\mathcal D_p$,
and $\mathcal D_p\ne\R^{\R}/p$.

statements.label: prop:well-defined
statements.statement_latex:
\label{prop:well-defined}
If $[f]_p=[g]_p$ and $D_f,D_g\in p$, then $[f']_p=[g']_p$.
Moreover, $\mathcal D_p$ is a subfield of the ultrapower and
$\partial[f]_p=[f']_p$ is a derivation from it to the ultrapower.

statements.label: lem:obstruction
statements.statement_latex:
\label{lem:obstruction}
Suppose $f:\R\to(0,1]$ has this property: whenever $T\in p$, $x\in T^*$
and $\delta>0$, there exists
\[
 y\in (T-x)\cap(0,\delta)
 \quad\text{such that}\quad f(x+y)<f(x)/2.
\]
Then every $g$ equivalent to $f$ is discontinuous at every point of a
$p$-large set. In particular $[f]_p\notin\mathcal D_p$.

Definition~\ref{def:transformation}, a transformation between the four
frameworks of Definition~\ref{def:four} exists if and only if

For a singleton action alphabet, no such transformation exists,
